title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The manuscript studies the structure at infinity of the moduli multiplicities M_{g,ν}. Y is a compactified moduli multiplicity (an orbifold or analytic stack) and Θ is the normal-crossings divisor at infinity. D' is a codimension-d stratum, factoring through Θ^{(d)}, with open part D'^*. P_{D'^*} is the punctured normal bundle: the complement of the coordinate hyperplanes in the normal bundle over D'^*, a torus bundle. On the previous page, formula (239) asserts an equivalence of fundamental groupoids, canonical up to unique isomorphism, Π_1 P_{D'^*} → Π_1 V^*_{D',Y}. Here V^*_{D',Y} is the trace of a tubular neighbourhood of D' on Y^* = Y \ Θ. This is the 'local structure at infinity' of the Teichmüller tower: the boundary fundamental groupoids, i.e. tangential base points at a stratum.

This page. To make (239) concrete, Grothendieck asks for an open embedding (240) V_{D',Y} ↪ N_{D',Y}, a tubular neighbourhood in the differentiable sense, not the analytic one. Its composite with D' → V_{D',Y} should be the zero section. It should also induce the identity on normal bundles along the zero section. The text writes 'Y → V_{D',Y}', but the sense requires D' → V.

He states that such an embedding should exist for genuine paracompact analytic spaces, by the classical C^∞ tubular neighbourhood theorem. It does not exist in general for multiplicities.

Counterexample. Take E^1 = {y=0} ⊂ E^2 (complex) with Z acting through the transvection (x,y) ↦ (x+y, y). Set D' = [E^1/Z] and Y = [E^2/Z].
- Z fixes E^1 pointwise and acts trivially on the normal direction.
- On T_Y|_{D'}, however, Z acts by the unipotent matrix (1 1; 0 1).
- So the extension 0 → T_{D'} → T_Y|_{D'} → N → 0 of Z-equivariant bundles is non-split.
- Along the zero section of any vector bundle this extension is canonically split.
- Hence no equivariant tubular embedding into the normal bundle exists.

He then remarks that for ordinary manifolds or analytic spaces, when such an immersion exists, it is a homotopy equivalence and so induces an equivalence on π_1. The next page uses this to build V^*_{D',Y} → P_{D'^*} (241) and the map on π_1 (242), noting that connectedness problems need extra hypotheses.

So the page serves one purpose: justifying the comparison between the punctured tubular neighbourhood of a boundary stratum and the punctured normal bundle. This comparison is the basis of tangential base points at infinity of M_{g,ν}.
errors: The text reads 'composée avec Y → V_{D',Y}'. The intended map must be D' → V_{D',Y} (the zero-section condition), so this is a slip of the pen or a misreading.

The counterexample works only because the stabilizer Z is infinite, so the action is not proper. For multiplicities with finite stabilizers (proper étale groupoids, as for the Deligne–Mumford M̄_{g,ν}), averaging splits the extension and equivariant tubular neighbourhoods do exist (linearization of proper groupoids). The obstruction he exhibits is therefore irrelevant to the actual M̄_{g,ν} case, and the page does not draw this distinction.

The claim that the tubular immersion is a homotopy equivalence is stated as 'assez clair' without proof. It is standard for manifolds, but the restriction to the complements of Θ (needed for (241)) requires compatibility of the tubular map with the stratification, which is only addressed on the next page.

ideas.what: Differentiable tubular neighbourhood of a boundary stratum, embedded in its normal bundle, with zero-section and identity-on-normal-bundle normalisation
ideas.modern_name: Tubular neighbourhood theorem (C^∞); exponential map adapted to a normal-crossings stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Milnor (classical); for stratified versions Mather and Thom

ideas.what: Failure of tubular neighbourhoods for stacks or multiplicities with infinite isotropy: the unipotent transvection action of Z gives a non-split extension of T_{D'} by N
ideas.modern_name: Non-linearizability of non-proper Lie groupoids / actions; obstruction via non-split equivariant tangent extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Linearization theory: Weinstein (2000), Zung (2006), Crainic–Struchiner (2013) for proper groupoids; failure for non-proper actions is folklore

ideas.what: Comparison of the π_1 or fundamental groupoid of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of a boundary stratum with that of the punctured normal bundle (torus bundle)
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points at boundary strata; specialization of fundamental groups via deformation to the normal cone
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989) for tangential base points; Ihara–Nakamura, Nakamura for the boundary of M_{g,n}; Grothendieck–Murre for tame π_1 at a normal-crossings divisor
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the 'structure à l'infini' of the Teichmüller tower without this technical detail

missed.claim: Grothendieck notes explicitly that the differentiable tubular-neighbourhood construction behind the 'tangential base point' comparison breaks down for multiplicities with infinite isotropy. He gives a concrete unipotent counterexample. This is an early, explicit awareness that comparison maps at infinity for stacks need properness or finite stabilizers. The fact itself is standard today.
missed.quote: l'extension des fibrés vectoriels différentiables définie par les plongements D' ↪ V_{D',Y} ⊂ Y – n'est pas scindable donc pas celle définie par la section nulle d'un fibré
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical rather than mathematical. It documents that Grothendieck worked through the topological foundations of tangential base points on moduli stacks, before Deligne's 1989 treatment and Nakamura's work. The mathematics itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a technical foundational step: a tubular neighbourhood into the normal bundle, plus a simple counterexample for non-proper stack actions. Both are standard to specialists today. Its interest is historical, as a detail of Grothendieck's development of tangential base points at infinity of M_{g,ν}.
transcription_corrections: 'Y → V_{D',Y}' should probably be read as (or meant as) 'D' → V_{D',Y}'.

The passage 'Se [?] [?] [?] dans ces dans le cas des vrais espaces analytiques paracompacts – i.e. sans [?] dans le cas des multiplicités' likely reads 'Ce [plongement] devrait exister toujours dans le cas des vrais espaces analytiques paracompacts – mais non dans le cas des multiplicités'.
'– est pas scindable' should read '– n'est pas scindable'.
'd'un fibré [?]' is likely 'd'un fibré linéaire' or 'vectoriel'.

'lorsqu'on dispose d'une telle immersion [?] cette condition = de différentiabilité' is likely 'd'une telle immersion (cet[te] condition de différentiabilité)'. The marginal insertion 'des variétés ou espaces analytiques ordinaires' qualifies the case considered.
